title: continuous-batcher-scheduler-tuning-queueing-fairness-starvation-timeouts
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: users observed tail latency spikes and occasional request starvation under mixed workloads (many short chat requests + a few long completion requests). This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness and starvation prevention while preserving throughput. Changes include a bounded max_wait_time for the batching window, per-queue fairness weights, a starvation detector that prioritizes long-waiting queues, and safer defaults for backpressure and eviction. Key outcomes: reduced p99 latency for short-chat workloads by ~22% under mixed load, eliminated observed starvation scenarios in internal stress tests, and added feature flags and metrics to allow staged rollout and rollback. Detailed changes: 1) Add config max_wait_time_ms (default 12ms) to bound how long a request may be queued waiting to form a batch; previously batches could delay up to 50ms under low batching opportunities which caused tail spikes. 2) Introduce per_queue_weight and priority_buckets so the scheduler can tune fairness between low-latency short requests and throughput-oriented long requests. 3) Implement starvation_threshold_ms and a lightweight FIFO escalation path: queues with requests older than starvation_threshold_ms are temporarily escalated and guaranteed a batch within escalation_timeout_ms. 4) Add dynamic_batch_window_ms heuristic that shrinks the batching window for low-latency queues when GPU occupancy is low. 5) Improve KV cache interaction: ensure evicted requests do not cause unnecessary KV cache thrashing by tagging cacheable prefixes and preferring cache-warm batches. 6) Backpressure: introduce queue_backpressure_limit and backpressure_action (reject|delay|route-to-fallback) to avoid unbounded queue growth under overload. 7) Observability: new metrics continuous_batcher.queue_wait_ms_histogram, continuous_batcher.starvation_escalations_total, continuous_batcher.per_queue_batch_size, and dashboards updated. 8) Feature flags and runtime knobs added for gradual rollout (ff.continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2). Testing & rollout: unit + integration tests added for scheduler heuristics, synthetic mixed-load benchmarks included in perf-canary with simulated KV cache hits/misses, and canary rollout plan described in PR checklist. Backwards compatibility: defaults chosen to be conservative; clusters can opt-in to aggressive settings via flags. See release_notes for user-facing changes. Checklist: - [x] Implement scheduler changes - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Add perf canary scenarios - [x] Add metrics and dashboards - [x] Feature flag gated rollout - [x] Docs note for runtime config knobs

release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler: added configurable max_wait_time_ms, per-queue fairness weights, starvation prevention/escalation, and backpressure options. Default settings chosen to reduce short-request tail latency while preserving throughput. Feature-flagged rollout. Metrics and dashboards added.
perf_regression_test_results: throughput: sustained throughput within 3% of baseline at 95% GPU utilization
kv-cache-stability: cache hit rate improved 4% in mixed eviction scenario
notes_for_ops: Ops: ff.continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 is feature-flag gated. Recommended rollout: enable in canary pool for 48h, monitor continuous_batcher.starvation_escalations_total and p99 tail latency, then roll to 20% fleet. If starvation_escalations_total increases unexpectedly, revert flag and investigate backlog characteristics.
author_comments: This PR is conservative by default to avoid impacting long-running batch jobs. Tunables allow SREs to dial-in fairness/latency tradeoffs per workload. Happy to split out smaller follow-ups (e.g., adaptive weight tuning) if reviewers prefer incremental changes.
